one_line_reason: Two placebo-controlled RCTs dosed single-ingredient Schisandra chinensis extract alone and found muscle-strength/fatigue benefits, with two more positive RCTs in combination products for glycemic control and stress.

selected.intervention: Schisandra chinensis (SC) extract alone, oral, 12 weeks
selected.primary_outcome: quadriceps muscle strength (QMS) and resting lactate level
selected.why_selected: clean single-ingredient RCT with a clear dose and a significant strength/lactate benefit.

selected.population: adults over 50 with relatively low muscle mass, doing low-intensity exercise (n=54)
selected.intervention: Schisandra chinensis Baillon extract (SCe) alone, oral, 12 weeks, alongside daily walking
selected.primary_outcome: knee extensor/handgrip strength and muscle mass
selected.why_selected: second clean single-ingredient RCT with a stated dose; strength improved significantly but muscle mass did not, giving a more nuanced positive-and-null picture.

selected.population: adults with hyperglycemia, fasting glucose 100-140 mg/dL (n=80)
selected.intervention: Omija (Schisandra chinensis) extract mixed with soybean (OSM), oral, 12 weeks
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (product described only as OSM mixture)
selected.primary_outcome: fasting/postprandial glucose, insulin, fructosamine, LDL cholesterol
selected.why_selected: adds a metabolic/glycemic outcome distinct from muscle strength, though the product is a schisandra-soybean mixture rather than schisandra alone.

selected.population: adults aged 18-65 with high perceived stress (n=186)
selected.intervention: multi-herb formula (Rhodiola, holy basil, and Schisandra chinensis; VL-G-A57), oral, 60 days
selected.primary_outcome: Perceived Stress Scale score; sleep quality, mood, anxiety
selected.why_selected: large, well-powered recent RCT (2026) showing a stress-related benefit, though schisandra is only one of three herbs in the formula.

blockers: Two of the four selected trials are combination products (schisandra + soybean; schisandra + Rhodiola + holy basil), so the effect cannot be cleanly isolated to schisandra alone.

The two clean single-ingredient trials studied muscle strength specifically in older adults or post-menopausal women doing structured exercise, not general supplement users, and one found no muscle-mass benefit despite a strength gain.
No trial ties its dose to a specific standardized extract ratio (e.g., % schisandrin), so mapping 1 g or 1000 mg/day to catalog label potency is uncertain.

excluded_pmids.reason: Preclinical (animal-model) meta-analysis of Schisandra chinensis for muscle atrophy; not human evidence.
Preclinical (animal-model) meta-analysis of Schisandra chinensis for liver injury; not human evidence.

Meta-analysis of traditional Chinese medicine multi-herb formulas for chronic urticaria; schisandra chinensis is listed only as one of many frequently-used herbs across different formulas, not isolated or dosed.
Chemistry/extraction-methods review of schisandra polysaccharides; not a clinical efficacy study.

Systematic review of gut microbiota changes across several different single-herb obesity trials; the Schisandra chinensis study within it affected gut microbiota composition but showed no significant change in anthropometry or laboratory biomarkers, and no trial-level detail is given.

Narrative systematic review of medicinal plants and the gut-brain axis in mental health; only vaguely suggests schisandra's gut-microbiota interaction 'could mediate' benefits, with no direct efficacy data.
General narrative history/future-perspectives review of plant adaptogens as a class; not a focused schisandra efficacy trial.

RCT of Saengmaeksan, a three-herb combination (Ophiopogon/Lirio platyphylla, Panax ginseng, and Schisandra chinensis) tested with high-intensity training; effect cannot be isolated to schisandra alone.
